prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key commitments and measures (max 500 words)

Economy, tax and pensions
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish the main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament.
- Maintain rates of Income Tax and VAT; raise at least £6bn/year by tackling avoidance/evasion.
- Triple Lock Plus: uprate both State Pension and pensioner personal allowance by the highest of inflation, earnings or 2.5%.
- Maintain National Living Wage at two‑thirds of median earnings (forecast ~£13/hour).

Families, childcare and welfare
- 30 hours free childcare from 9 months to school age by Sept 2025.
- Move Child Benefit to a household test: taper between £120k–£160k combined income.
- Family Hubs in every English local authority.
- Welfare reform: redesign PIP; tighten Work Capability Assessment from Sept 2025; shift fit notes to work/health professionals; tougher sanctions after 12 months; Fraud Bill giving DWP HMRC‑like powers; complete Universal Credit rollout.

Education, skills and youth
- Mandatory National Service at 18 (paid, competitive military year or part‑time civic service).
- 100,000 additional apprenticeships, funded by closing poor‑outcome university courses.
- Advanced British Standard for 16–19; statutory school‑day mobile phone bans; two hours PE weekly; expand teacher bonuses; 60,000 more SEND places and 15 new special free schools.

Health and social care
- NHS spending to rise above inflation annually; recruit +92,000 nurses and +28,000 doctors.
- Pharmacy First expansion; build/modernise 250 GP surgeries; +50 Community Diagnostic Centres.
- Dental plan: 2.5m more NHS appointments; service requirement for new dentists; “golden hellos” and dental vans.
- Patient choice across NHS, charity and independent providers at NHS cost.
- £3.4bn NHS tech plan: NHS App as front door, AI for imaging, Federated Data Platform; cut 5,500 managers.
- Women’s Health actions; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; mental health: school teams to 100% by 2030, nationwide early support hubs, +50% Talking Therapies.

Crime, justice and policing
- +8,000 neighbourhood police; hotspot policing; Martyn’s Law.
- Tougher sentences for serious violence, sexual offences and domestic murders; expand tagging/community payback.
- Four new prisons (completing 20,000 places); speed up courts; anti‑fraud measures; updated protest powers.

Borders and immigration
- Legal, binding cap on work and family visas with annual Parliament vote; raise salary thresholds; pre‑travel health checks and higher/loss of IHS discounts.
- Process asylum claims in six months, end hotel use; regular removals to Rwanda; pursue returns deals; seek updates to international asylum rules.

Defence and foreign policy
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; £10bn munitions; defence R&D minimum 5% of budget plus 2% to scale; National Defence and Resilience Plan.
- Veterans Bill; veterans’ benefits and ID use in elections.

Energy and net zero
- Net zero 2050 maintained; annual North Sea oil and gas licensing; new gas plants for security.
- Treble offshore wind; approve first two SMR fleets within 100 days; progress Wylfa; halve nuclear approval times; CCUS clusters; £1.1bn Green Industries Growth Accelerator.
- Maintain windfall tax to 2028–29 (subject to prices); energy efficiency vouchers; review standing charges; Pumpwatch; no new green levies or road pricing.

Housing and planning
- 1.6m homes; scrap nutrient neutrality (with mitigation fees) to unlock ~100k; fast‑track brownfield; urban densification; development corporations; renew Affordable Homes Programme.
- Permanent Stamp Duty relief for first‑time buyers up to £425k; new Help to Buy; temporary CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants; complete leasehold reform; Renters Reform with S21 abolition after court reforms.

Transport and infrastructure
- Redirect £36bn HS2 savings to local projects; extend £2 bus fare for full Parliament; Rail Reform Bill creating Great British Railways; nationwide pay‑as‑you‑go contactless.
- Backing drivers: ban road pricing by local/national government; reverse London ULEZ expansion; local referendums for LTNs/20mph; £8.3bn for potholes.

Communities, union and devolution
- Town endowments, Community Ownership Fund, more Freeports/Investment Zones; extended UK Shared Prosperity Fund; further support and specific projects for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

Equality, sex and gender
- Clarify in law that Equality Act “sex” means biological sex; protect single‑sex services and NHS accommodation; implement Cass Review; require schools to follow gender‑questioning guidance and share materials with parents.

Rural, farming, fisheries, environment
- Increase UK‑wide farming budget by £1bn over Parliament; legal food security target and index; 50% public procurement from local/higher‑standard food; fast‑track farm infrastructure; five‑year tapered seasonal visa scheme.
- Replicate £100m Seafood Fund; maintain high flood‑defence funding; Plan for Water reforms, tougher sanctions; tree/peat programmes; 11th National Park; waste crime penalties; constrain new incinerators.

Culture and sport
- Continue grassroots sports facilities funding; Independent Football Regulator; maintain competitive creative tax incentives; BBC funding review; night‑time economy review.
